Bug_Details: Use of Joda-Time's DateTime.toDateTime(), Duration.toDuration(), Instant.toInstant(), Interval.toInterval(), and Period.toPeriod() are not allowed. Joda-Time’s DateTime.toDateTime(), Duration.toDuration(), Instant.toInstant(), Interval.toInterval(), and Period.toPeriod() are always unnecessary, since they simply ‘return this’. There is no reason to ever call them.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is present in the code where the Joda-Time's Duration.toDuration() method is called on a duration object. This method is not necessary as it simply returns 'this' and hence it is unnecessary to call it.

Trigger_Explanation: The showBug() method in the JodaToSelfBug class returns a Joda Time Duration object, but the original test code asserts that the duration is not null. This assertion will fail when the bug is triggered, returning the Joda Time Duration object instead of null.
Model_Explanation: The bug is present in the code. The method showBug() creates a Duration object and then immediately calls toDuration() on it. This is unnecessary because the toDuration() method simply returns the object itself. This is a violation of the bug rule 'JodaToSelf', which states that the Joda-Time's DateTime.toDateTime(), Duration.toDuration(), Instant.toInstant(), Interval.toInterval(), and Period.toPeriod() methods are not allowed. They are always unnecessary because they simply'return this'.
